scope: Private Windows installation; one physical computer, account and CPU resource domain. Real Qwen3-32B work survives a controlled Windows status-file read lock. Independent-host, GPU, public-economic and OS-isolation qualification remain open.
validation_notes: All 160 distinct automated cases were rerun locally for this patch. The nine-second real fault campaign is additional acceptance evidence, not a unit fixture.
The CI application job runs three model-independent browser journeys. Seven other journeys and the actual 32B lock campaign use the original local installation and models.

A separate final check used the extracted source package CLI against both actual contributor profiles, verified current READY/fresh status, rendered the 0.10.1 interface and checked all nine applied migration hashes without writes.
Old v0.10 evidence, tag and package remain unchanged; its complete fault campaign is historical evidence, not a rerun under this patch.

Replacement EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES is treated as telemetry degradation only after the new snapshot was written and temporary-file cleanup succeeded. Persistent replacement permission errors can also degrade telemetry. Other storage errors and child exits still drain the contributor.
boundaries: one physical Windows CPU host and account, not independent providers
diagnostic status is not execution/payment authority
no Windows Job Object/service or hostile-engine OS sandbox yet
independent GPU/Linux/WAN/NAT/relay and sustained recovery qualification
independent observed costs, successful economics, approved issuance, public work verification, distributed continuity and cash settlement
